proof:
Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).
Source: parent proof, Setting ("S(v, v′) := D²ψ(x)[v, v′], symmetric … ψ ∈ C²"). The cited Mathlib lemma ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt (Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric) is not importable from GMT.Ch02.Submission, and a childless node may not add imports, so the classical second-difference proof is given.
Setting. Write Dψ := fderiv ℝ ψ and D²ψ := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ). Fix x ∈ V and v, w ∈ ℝⁿ, and put d := D²ψ(x) v w − D²ψ(x) w v ∈ ℝᴺ.
1. (Regularity.) V is open and ψ is C² on V, so Dψ is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen) and D²ψ is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). For every z ∈ V, ψ is differentiable at z with derivative Dψ(z), and Dψ is differentiable at z with derivative D²ψ(z) (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt, V being a neighbourhood of z).
2. (Choice of scales.) Let ε > 0. By continuity of D²ψ at x and openness of V there is δ > 0 with Metric.ball x δ ⊆ V and ‖D²ψ(z) − D²ψ(x)‖ ≤ ε for all z ∈ ball x δ. Put t := δ/(‖v‖ + ‖w‖ + 1) > 0. For r, s ∈ [0, t], ‖r v + s w‖ ≤ t(‖v‖ + ‖w‖) < δ, so x + r v + s w ∈ ball x δ ⊆ V.
3. (Inner estimate.) Fix s ∈ [0, t] and define k(r) := Dψ(x + r v + s w) w − r • D²ψ(x) v w for r ∈ [0, t]. By the chain rule (Dψ differentiable at x + r v + s w, the affine curve r ↦ x + r v + s w has velocity v, evaluation at w is continuous linear), k has derivative k′(r) = D²ψ(x + r v + s w) v w − D²ψ(x) v w = (D²ψ(x + r v + s w) − D²ψ(x)) v w, and ‖k′(r)‖ ≤ ‖D²ψ(x + r v + s w) − D²ψ(x)‖ ‖v‖ ‖w‖ ≤ ε ‖v‖ ‖w‖ (operator-norm bounds, step 2). By the mean value inequality (norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment' on [0, t]), ‖k(t) − k(0)‖ ≤ ε ‖v‖ ‖w‖ t, i.e.
   ‖Dψ(x + t v + s w) w − Dψ(x + s w) w − t • D²ψ(x) v w‖ ≤ ε t ‖v‖ ‖w‖ for every s ∈ [0, t].
4. (Outer estimate.) Define g(s) := ψ(x + t v + s w) − ψ(x + s w) − (s t) • D²ψ(x) v w for s ∈ [0, t]. By the chain rule g has derivative g′(s) = Dψ(x + t v + s w) w − Dψ(x + s w) w − t • D²ψ(x) v w, so ‖g′(s)‖ ≤ ε t ‖v‖ ‖w‖ by step 3, and the mean value inequality gives ‖g(t) − g(0)‖ ≤ ε t² ‖v‖ ‖w‖. Since g(t) − g(0) = Δ − t² • D²ψ(x) v w with the second difference Δ := ψ(x + t v + t w) − ψ(x + t v) − ψ(x + t w) + ψ(x), we get ‖Δ − t² • D²ψ(x) v w‖ ≤ ε t² ‖v‖ ‖w‖.
5. (Exchange v and w.) Δ is unchanged when v and w are exchanged (x + t v + t w = x + t w + t v), and steps 3–4 hold verbatim with v and w exchanged (same δ and t, since t(‖v‖ + ‖w‖) is symmetric). Hence also ‖Δ − t² • D²ψ(x) w v‖ ≤ ε t² ‖v‖ ‖w‖. (In a single Lean theorem, state steps 3–4 once as a `have` quantified over the pair (v₁, v₂) with ‖v₁‖ + ‖v₂‖ = ‖v‖ + ‖w‖, and instantiate it with (v, w) and (w, v); no helper declaration is needed.)
6. (Conclusion.) By the triangle inequality t² ‖d‖ ≤ 2 ε t² ‖v‖ ‖w‖, so ‖d‖ ≤ 2 ε ‖v‖ ‖w‖ because t > 0. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, ‖d‖ = 0, i.e. fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x v w = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x w v. ∎
key_steps: Dψ is C¹ on V, D²ψ is continuous on V, and ψ, Dψ are differentiable at every point of V.
For ε > 0 pick δ with ball x δ ⊆ V and ‖D²ψ(z) − D²ψ(x)‖ ≤ ε there, and t := δ/(‖v‖+‖w‖+1).
Two applications of the mean value inequality give ‖Δ − t² D²ψ(x)[v,w]‖ ≤ ε t²‖v‖‖w‖ for the second difference Δ = ψ(x+tv+tw) − ψ(x+tv) − ψ(x+tw) + ψ(x).
Δ is symmetric in (v, w), so ‖D²ψ(x)[v,w] − D²ψ(x)[w,v]‖ ≤ 2ε‖v‖‖w‖ for all ε > 0, hence equality.
